outline.description: This chapter introduces the motivation behind ultra-low-bit language models. It explains why modern LLMs are expensive to run, why reducing numerical precision matters, and how BitNet b1.58 fits into the broader effort to make large models faster, cheaper, and more energy-efficient without sacrificing quality.

outline.description: Before studying BitNet b1.58, students need the technical background behind quantized neural networks and Transformer-based LLMs. This chapter reviews standard Transformer components, quantization basics, and the original BitNet framework that BitNet b1.58 builds upon.

outline.description: This chapter presents the main model proposed in the paper. It explains what BitNet b1.58 is, how its weights and activations are represented, and why ternary weights offer a stronger modeling capability than strict binary weights while preserving most of the efficiency benefits.
subtopics: Definition of BitNet b1.58

outline.description: This chapter provides a detailed treatment of the paper’s quantization method. It walks through the absmean weight quantization function, the activation quantization strategy, and the implementation choices that make the model practical for training and hardware optimization.

outline.description: BitNet b1.58 is not just a quantization scheme; it is packaged in a practical LLM architecture aligned with the open-source LLaMA ecosystem. This chapter explains the architectural choices and why compatibility with popular software stacks matters for adoption.

outline.description: This chapter explains how the authors performed fair comparisons between BitNet b1.58 and full-precision LLaMA-style baselines. It covers datasets, token budgets, benchmark tasks, and the difference between intrinsic metrics like perplexity and downstream zero-shot accuracy.

outline.description: This chapter analyzes the paper’s central empirical finding: BitNet b1.58 can match full-precision LLM performance starting around 3B parameters under the same training setup. It also explains the meaning of the reported Pareto improvements and how scaling changes the performance gap.

outline.chapter_title: 8. Systems Performance: Memory, Latency, Throughput, and Energy
outline.description: This chapter focuses on the systems-level benefits of BitNet b1.58. It explains how reduced precision affects runtime memory, token generation latency, throughput, and arithmetic energy, and why these gains often grow as models get larger.

outline.chapter_title: 9. A New Scaling Law for Cost-Effective LLMs
outline.description: One of the paper’s most important ideas is that BitNet b1.58 changes the relationship between model size and deployment cost. This chapter explores the paper’s proposed new scaling perspective, in which larger 1.58-bit models can be more efficient than much smaller FP16 models.

outline.chapter_title: 10. Scaling with More Data: The 2T Token Experiment
outline.description: This chapter studies whether BitNet b1.58 remains competitive when trained with far more data. It uses the paper’s 2-trillion-token experiment to examine generalization and the interaction between model precision and data scaling.

outline.description: The final chapter expands beyond the reported experiments to examine how BitNet b1.58 could influence future research and deployment. It discusses mixture-of-experts models, long-context inference, mobile deployment, and hardware co-design for 1-bit LLMs.
